profile.summary: scBERT is a pretrained deep language model for annotating cell types in single-cell RNA-seq data. It is first pre-trained on large amounts of unlabelled scRNA-seq data to learn gene-gene interactions, then fine-tuned on a labelled reference; the fine-tuned model takes a normalised expression profile and outputs the cell type of each cell, and can flag novel cell types by thresholding prediction confidence.

summary_quotes.text: we present a pretrained deep neural network-based model scBERT (single-cell Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers)
scBERT obtains a general understanding of gene-gene interaction by being pre-trained on huge amounts of unlabeled scRNA-seq data
The expected output of model inference is the cell type of each individual cell.
The detection of novel cell type can be done by thresholding the predicted probabilities.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: scBERT follows BERT's pre-train and fine-tune approach with a Performer encoder. Expression values are binned into a small number of tokens (num_tokens, default 7 in the README) and combined with a gene embedding; predict.py uses Gene2vec encoding for genes by default and a sequence of 16906 genes plus one. The default encoder has 6 layers, 10 heads and a 200-dimensional embedding. For annotation a classifier head is trained on top during fine-tuning.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One pre-trained checkpoint is offered through a Weixin Drive link, with no version label or checksum. Users fine-tune it on their own labelled data, so every annotation result depends on the fine-tuning data. predict.py sets bin_num to 5 by default and builds the model with num_tokens = bin_num + 2 = 7, which matches the README's default num_tokens of 7 (the README calls this the number of bins). A result should name the repository commit, the checkpoint source and the fine-tuning data.

strengths.text: Pre-trained on unlabelled data and then fine-tuned, so it does not depend on curated marker gene lists (authors' framing).

quotes.text: existing annotation methods typically suffer from lack of curated marker gene lists

strengths.text: Can flag novel cell types by thresholding prediction confidence.
Small default configuration (6 layers, embedding size 200) with documented hyperparameter ranges.

limitations.text: Needs fine-tuning on labelled data before it annotates anything.
Old, pinned dependencies (torch 1.8.1, transformers 4.6.1, Python 3.6.8 badge).
Checkpoint and data are on Weixin and Google Drive links with no licence or version; the README says all rights reserved.
Gene symbols must be revised to a fixed 2020 NCBI Gene release, and run times are slow on a desktop (about 25 minutes for 10,000 cells, as stated).

quotes.text: Exptected run time for infering 10,000 cells on a "normal" desktop computer is about 25 minutes.
